meta.note: English translation overlay for items.json. Purely presentational: all item/badge IDs and backend records are unchanged. Names follow the official Scout Association of Hong Kong English Scout Training Scheme.
meta.source: Official English Scout Training Scheme (Scout Association of Hong Kong) — FullVersion-en.pdf and pdf-en award sheets

L1.purpose_en: Help new members know the Scout Movement and the Patrol System
L1.description_en: Complete within 1.5 months of joining; issued by the Scout Leader

L1-01.detail_en: Know the Scout Movement, the Scout Promise, Law, Motto and the Patrol System.

L1-02.detail_en: Complete the Safe from Harm related requirements.

L2.purpose_en: Experience & exposure: a first taste of Scouting; suggested 6 months
L2.description_en: From age 11; Scouts aged 13 or above may complete only the Outdoor Challenge sections of the Pathfinder and Standard Awards, then proceed directly to the Advanced Award

L2-01.detail_en: Take part in an overnight Scout camp; pack a rucksack for a two-day-one-night camp; use potentially dangerous gear safely; maintain camping gear.

L2-02.detail_en: Complete a journey of at least 8 km on foot or 12 km by bicycle/boat; know maps and 10 legend symbols; pack a rucksack for a 1-day countryside journey.

L2-03.detail_en: Demonstrate the reef knot, figure-of-eight knot, clove hitch, half hitch, overhand knot, bowline, sheet bend, round turn & two half hitches and timber hitch, and learn how to maintain ropes.

L2-04.detail_en: Know the safety guidelines for outdoor activities and the Country Code; complete one of: tracking signs, park orienteering, or communication with codes.

L2-05.detail_en: Know the safety rules for sea activities and pass the Association swimming test; compulsory for Sea Scouts.

L2-06.detail_en: State the safety rules for airports and aircraft; complete one of: an outdoor air activity, naming aircraft parts, or basic aircraft identification; compulsory for Air Scouts.

L2-07.detail_en: Take part in a patrol activity themed on sports or physical fitness.

L2-08.detail_en: Know your patrol yell and use it in an activity.

L2-09.detail_en: Attend one patrol meeting and state its purpose.

L2-10.detail_en: Share daily-life examples of applying the Scout Promise, Law and Motto; and take part in a Scouts' Own.

L2-11.detail_en: Demonstrate how to handle nosebleed, burns, scalds, cuts and thorns; complete at least 4 hours of approved service and keep a record.

L2-12.detail_en: Introduce to your patrol the community facilities near your home or troop base.

L2-13.detail_en: Visit an exhibition or place on the theme of nature, environment or habitat.

L2-14.detail_en: Understand the difference between weather and climate and their effects on outdoor activities.

L3.purpose_en: Knowledge & cognition: building a sense of achievement; suggested 6 months
L3.description_en: For Scouts who have completed the Scout Pathfinder Award, or aged 13+ with the Membership Badge and the Pathfinder Outdoor Challenge section

L3-01.detail_en: Participate in and share a record of a camp; pitch, pack and store a tent; complete at least 4 camping gadgets; light a fire outdoors and cook.

L3-02.detail_en: Complete a journey of at least 12 km on foot or 18 km by bicycle/boat; understand map scales & distances, setting a map, and fixing position with map and compass.

L3-03.detail_en: Demonstrate square, diagonal and figure-of-eight lashings, shear lashing and shear legs; follow pioneering safety rules; complete a pioneering project.

L3-04.detail_en: Complete the Pathfinder Award outdoor activities; attain an outdoor-activities proficiency badge not previously attained; complete city-tracking or a communication activity.

L3-05.detail_en: Complete the Pathfinder Award sea activities; attain the Oarsman badge; take part in one designated sea activity.

L3-06.detail_en: Complete the Pathfinder Award air activities; attain the Basic Air Activity Badge; complete either the aviation-safety or the effect-of-wind-on-flight item.

L3-07.detail_en: Attain a physical-fitness proficiency badge not previously attained; or plan and cook a balanced meal.

L3-08.detail_en: Take part in a campfire or lantern night, and complete one art, creativity or technology option.

L3-09.detail_en: Take part in one patrol activity (indoor or outdoor).

L3-10.detail_en: Take part in a Scouts' Own, and introduce a religion or share a belief.

L3-11.detail_en: Learn basic first-aid diagnosis and how to call emergency services; pack a personal first-aid kit for a 1-day outdoor activity; complete at least 8 hours of approved service.

L3-12.detail_en: Participate in or watch local cultural practices or traditional festivals.

L3-13.detail_en: Introduce a foreign activity or culture.

L3-14.detail_en: Introduce food chains, biological networks and the ecological cycle.

L3-15.detail_en: Introduce the measurement of wind speed and direction, or cloud formation and the 10 basic cloud types.

L3-16.detail_en: Introduce the effects of natural disasters, or know the Leave No Trace principles.

L3-17.detail_en: Take part, as a Scout, in an exchange activity with another troop or organisation.

L4.purpose_en: Deepening knowledge: developing responsibility; suggested 12 months
L4.description_en: For Scouts who have completed the Scout Standard Award, or aged 13+ with the Membership Badge and the Outdoor Challenge sections of the Pathfinder and Standard Awards

L4-01.detail_en: Help plan and take part in a camp; complete at least 6 camping gadgets; take part in backwoods cooking.

L4-02.detail_en: Complete a two-day-one-night expedition of at least 20 km on foot or 30 km by bicycle/boat, or a dusk-to-dawn night hike; understand contour lines and finding directions without a compass.

L4-03.detail_en: Demonstrate the double sheet bend, fisherman's knot, rolling hitch, mousing, scaffold sling and common whipping; build two pioneering projects using at least 2 different lashings.

L4-04.detail_en: Complete the Standard Award outdoor activities; attain two of Camper, Explorer, Pioneer and Backwoods Cook (Pursuit).

L4-05.detail_en: Complete the Standard Award sea activities; attain the Boatman badge and one sea-activities proficiency badge.

L4-06.detail_en: Complete the Standard Award air activities; attain the Intermediate Air Activity Badge and learn aviation meteorology.

L4-07.detail_en: Attain a physical-fitness proficiency badge not previously attained; or carry out and record a 4–6 week physical training plan.

L4-08.detail_en: Attain an art, creativity or technology proficiency badge not previously attained, and complete one creation or performance.

L4-09.detail_en: Attend a Patrol Leaders' Council meeting and carry out one of its decisions.

L4-10.detail_en: Undertake a duty in the patrol, troop or group for at least 3 months, and complete a religious / spiritual-development option.

L4-11.detail_en: Pack a patrol first-aid kit for a two-day-one-night activity; demonstrate treatment of wounds, bleeding, heat stroke and heat exhaustion; plan community activities; complete at least 12 hours of service.

L4-12.detail_en: Attain a community-related badge, or introduce the District Council and Legislative Council, or take part in an inclusion activity.

L4-13.detail_en: Introduce an international organisation, or a Scout organisation of another country / region.

L4-14.detail_en: Introduce Hong Kong's habitats, species classification, diversity, distribution and endangered species.

L4-15.detail_en: Introduce the four seasons or the 24 solar terms, plus Hong Kong's climate or weather terminology.

L4-16.detail_en: Introduce sustainable development, or take part in at least one day / two occasions of environmental conservation work.

L4-17.detail_en: Take part in a challenging activity you have never attempted and introduce it to your patrol members.

L5.purpose_en: The highest award of the Scout Section: planning and leadership; suggested 12 months
L5.description_en: For Scouts who have completed the Scout Advanced Award, or aged 13+ holding the Membership Badge and the Advanced Award plus the Outdoor Challenge sections of the Pathfinder and Standard Awards

L5-01.detail_en: Plan and run an overnight wild camp; teach basic camping skills; produce a camp log.

L5-02.detail_en: Plan, complete and record a two-day-one-night expedition of at least 30 km; teach expedition skills and wild survival.

L5-03.detail_en: Plan and lead a pioneering project using at least 3 different lashings; teach knotting and rope care.

L5-04.detail_en: Complete the Advanced Award outdoor activities; plan and take part in a whole-day patrol outdoor activity.

L5-05.detail_en: Complete the Advanced Award sea activities; plan and take part in a sea journey of at least 6 hours.

L5-06.detail_en: Complete the Advanced Award air activities; after consulting the Scout Leader, complete two self-chosen air activities.

L5-07.detail_en: Attain a physical-fitness proficiency badge not previously attained, and plan a patrol sports or fitness activity.

L5-08.detail_en: Create and lead a campfire item, and complete one teaching or creation project.

L5-10.detail_en: Introduce the Scout Promise, Law and Motto; and lead a silent prayer, assist in a Scouts' Own, or attain the Religious Badge.

L5-11.detail_en: Attain one of First Aid, Fireman or Lifesaver (Service); discuss a community-participation activity; complete at least 16 hours of service.

L5-12.detail_en: Discuss a local current issue; and complete Tourism (Interest), communication with people with special needs, or a community survey.

L5-13.detail_en: Discuss an international issue; and complete JOTA/JOTI, an overseas exchange programme, or introduce foreign Scouting.

L5-14.detail_en: Attain an ecology-related proficiency badge or award not previously attained.

L5-15.detail_en: Teach a meteorological topic; and attain the Meteorologist (Interest) badge or study weather charts with a one-week record.

L5-16.detail_en: Introduce the impact of human activities on the environment; plan and lead an environmental conservation project.

L5-17.detail_en: Complete a challenging activity never attempted before and introduce it to your patrol members.

trainingPlan.title: Scout Section Training Programme (2017 1st Revision + 2026 Proficiency Badge Update)
trainingPlan.purpose: The Scout Section (ages 11–16) promotes physical, mental and spiritual development. Through the progressive awards and the proficiency badge scheme, together with the Patrol System, members learn by doing.
method: Patrol System: the patrol is the basic unit, led by the Patrol Leader
Progressive Awards: Pathfinder → Standard → Advanced → Chief Scout's, step by step

Proficiency Badges: Interest (green, troop-assessed, leader ticks), Pursuit (blue, district-assessed, member fills date and leader approves), Service (red, district-assessed), Instructor (yellow, teach others 3 months after attaining)
expected: Development across the six domains (moral, intellectual, physical, social, aesthetic and spiritual)
trainingPlan.progressFlow: Membership Badge → Scout Pathfinder Award → Scout Standard Award → Scout Advanced Award → Chief Scout's Award (each award consists of progress items; no stage badges)
trainingPlan.assessmentPrinciples: Interest badges may be assessed under the arrangement of the Scout Leader. Pursuit, Service and Instructor badges require the Scout Leader's approval of the assessment application, and assessment by an authorised representative of the Association, a Region or a District. First Aid, Fireman and Lifesaver all belong to the Service Group.
